newsitem.title: UK: East Europe 96/97 beet sugar output to fall - Licht.
newsitem.headline: East Europe 96/97 beet sugar output to fall - Licht.

text.p: Eastern European beet sugar output should be no more than 8.78 million tonnes in 1996/97, some 900,000 tonnes below the previous season, German statistician F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.

"A severe drought and no doubt increasing chaos in some areas have meant that we have had to mark down the total for this region once again," Licht said in its first estimate of the European beet sugar crop for 1996/97. In Russia, the area had been reduced after poor returns from sugar beet production while yields were expected to be down because of a low level of fertiliser application.
Licht pegged Russian output at 1.92 million tonnes from 2.23 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Output in Ukraine was unlikely to reach the 3.8 million tonnes produced in 1995/96 and should come in at a maximum of 2.7 to 2.8 million tonnes due to drought.
But Poland and the Czech Republic could buck the trend with higher production expected as a result of increased sowings.
Licht saw Polish output at 1.96 million tonnes from 1.72 million and that of the Czech Republic at 565,000 tonnes from 520,000 in 1995/96.
